metadata.title: Independent exact verification of the counterexample to Goemans' unsplittable-flow cost conjecture and of the 2026 lower-bound instances, with certified planarity and optimal pricing
metadata.description:
A seven-vertex instance announced in July 2026 refutes Goemans' conjecture that a feasible fractional single-source flow can be rounded to an unsplittable flow that loads no arc beyond x_a + d_max and costs no more than the fractional flow. We verify that instance, and eleven instances of the 2026 lower-bound series (among them the current general record of De la Fuente and the current planar record of Nikolenko), by exact rational enumeration with a library written from the statement of the conjecture, without running any verifier of their authors. The seven-vertex instance forces a violation of exactly 16/15 of d_max.

We prove that a separation linear program decides whether any nonnegative cost vector makes an instance a counterexample, that its optimum on the seven-vertex instance is 2/7 and is attained by the published prices, and that no single-terminal instance is a counterexample. A cutting-plane evaluator computes the frontier value, the violation forced by the best prices, exactly on instances with 131,072 routings. The eleven instances reproduce their claimed values to the last digit; the two 17-terminal instances are non-planar and the others planar, each decided by a checked certificate; and re-pricing gains nothing on any of them. Exact checks of Muffatti's subfamily of the symmetric three-terminal template, with forced violation 9/8 - (3/4) eps, and of Afrasyab's odd-cycle family on C5, whose 3,696 members all have frontier value at most 1, complete the computations. The theorems of the sources are not re-proved, and the two-terminal case remains open.

The counterexample instance is Rybin's; the current lower bounds are De la Fuente's (general) and Nikolenko's (planar); the value 9/8, both as a lower bound and as the supremum of the symmetric three-terminal family, is Muffatti's (note of 24 July 2026) and, independently, Nikolenko's; the four-terminal value (299 - 41 sqrt(41))/32 is Protti's (note of 23 July 2026) and Nikolenko's; no claim of priority or of a new bound is made. Source code, data and computational records: https://github.com/fsantibanezleal/CAOS_RESEARCH (problems/optimization-geometry/unsplittable-flow-cost).
metadata.version_notes: Adds the independent verification of eleven instances of the 2026 lower-bound series (values, planarity certificates, optimality of the prices), the frontier value with its exact evaluators, and the exact checks of the symmetric three-terminal and odd-cycle families. States each result of the series with its author and date (Rybin, Muffatti, Protti, Nikolenko, De la Fuente, Afrasyab) and corrects the status of the cost-free two-sided conjecture.
